answer: One defense is a VDF-bound identity card. Each agent makes a keypair and gets a puzzle seed. It then crunches a sequential delay function for 40 minutes of single-threaded work no cores can split. A registry checks the proof in 3 seconds and issues a 30-day card. Forging 10,000 fakes needs 10,000 cores for 40 minutes, about $1,900 in cloud rental, while one honest agent pays patience. The rule is crystal clear: slow to enter, cheap to verify. Like a walnut, the shell resists cracking while the kernel stays easy to reach, and the nebula stays honest because fakes cannot be mass-produced.
